chunks: (1) Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqdah narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Abdillah al-Muhammadi narrated to us from his book in Rajab of the year 268 AH, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl narrated to me, saying: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated to us from Is'haq ibn Ammar al-Sayrafi, who said: Isma'il ibn Ammar, the brother of Abu Abdillah, described his faith and belief, saying: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that you (describing them - meaning the Imams - one by one) until he reached Abu Abdillah, then he said: 'And Isma'il is [the Imam] after you.' He said: 'As for Isma'il, no.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS)
key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ عَمَّارٍ: Isma'il ibn Ammar, brother of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.الْإِمَامَةُ: Imamate, the leadership and authority of the Imams

ai.seo_question: Who was the designated Imam after Ja'far al-Sadiq according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the critical distinction between Isma'il ibn Ja'far's self-proclamation and the Imamate's divine designation (*nass*), a pivotal element in the Isma'ili-Shia split. The Imam’s concise correction, 'As for Isma'il, no,' underscores the principle that succession is determined by God’s decree rather than mere lineage or personal assertion, reinforcing the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in defining the line of Imams.
